A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same normalization-based dependency-parsing study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, appendices, and checklists are readable and support reliable matching across revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on six dependency-parsing datasets, including architecture ablations, fine-tuning results, and convergence analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds multilingual parsing, non-linguistic graph inference, GAT experiments, and revised depth experiments.

M1.justification: V2 extends the original one-hop parser with repeated biaffine–GAT blocks before the final scorer (Appendix C, Figure 5). Appendix B also introduces a non-linguistic adaptation using graph features, GAT processing, and sigmoid edge predictions without MST decoding. These change architecture and inference, while retaining the original normalization rule.

E1.justification: V2 retains the original six datasets and adds syntactic parsing in Arabic, Chinese, Italian, Japanese, Spanish, and Wolof. It also evaluates unlabeled graph inference on PCQM-Contact, CIFAR10 Superpixel, and QM9, substantially extending language, domain, and task coverage.

E2.justification: The Bhatt et al. baseline in Table 3 is retained. V2 additionally evaluates unnormalized biaffine–GAT parsers against their normalized counterparts on the original six datasets (Table 7), adding an architectural comparison family without expanding the named external baseline set.

E3.justification: The deep-BiLSTM experiment changes from 2,000 training steps in v1 Appendix B.2 to 20,000 in v2 Appendix D.2. Added experiments introduce mBERT for multilingual parsing and controlled GAT-depth evaluations with zero parser BiLSTM layers; non-linguistic evaluation uses unlabeled F1. These are substantive experimental-design changes, not merely additional disclosure.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses testing normalization across GAT refinement depths on linguistic and non-linguistic graphs. It also revises the deep-BiLSTM analysis with longer training and adds enEWT and SciDTB to that analysis. The original tagger, MLP-size, initialization, LayerNorm, and full-fine-tuning ablations remain.

E5.justification: The five-seed mean/standard-deviation and Wilcoxon reporting framework is retained, but v2 Appendix B specifies three seeds for the new non-linguistic experiments. The replacement depth plot also omits the p-values displayed in v1 Figure 5. The general five-seed statement and checklist are not reconciled with the three-seed exception.

E6.justification: Table 3 and the original supplementary tables retain their numerical results after relocation. V2 adds Tables 5–7, changes Figure 1's rank trajectories, and replaces the depth results under a longer training budget. New Table 6 reports CIFAR10 Superpixel F1 of 0.407 raw versus 0.531 normalized with one GAT layer, but 0.751 versus 0.703 with three, showing that the added findings include reversals.

T1.justification: Section 3 replaces Claim 1's Frobenius-norm covariance inequality with monotonicity of total variance measured by covariance trace. V2 explicitly defines nested truncated-SVD approximations and supplies a new trace/Loewner-order proof, avoiding v1's unjustified assertion that increasing rank adds a positive-semidefinite covariance increment.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusions broaden the work from one-hop dependency parsing to multilingual parsing, non-linguistic graph inference, and k-hop GAT parsing. Investigating GNN-based refinement changes from future work in v1 to a claimed confirmed extension in v2. The central normalization benefit and up-to-85% parameter-reduction claims are retained.

C2.justification: V2 interprets its new evidence as supporting language-independent and non-linguistic applicability, and discusses why multi-hop refinement offers less benefit for semantic than syntactic parsing. The depth discussion changes from sharp failures under short training to dataset-dependent instability after longer training. Appendix B interprets shrinking or reversing normalization advantages as further support for depth compensation.

D1.justification: V2 adds treebank split counts and source links, identifies the mBERT checkpoint, and documents graph-feature construction, coordinate concatenation, adjacency inputs, and approximate model sizes. The abstract's code pointer changes from an anonymous repository to the author's GitHub repository. Existing hardware, optimizer, and main-experiment compute disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: V2 retains the original 44 references and adds ten covering latent graph inference, GATs, graph benchmarks, multilingual Universal Dependencies, and ACE corpora. Section 2 adds a brief broader graph-inference framing, while the principal positioning relative to biaffine dependency parsers remains.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose remain intact. V2 makes localized language edits, standardizes BiLSTM-depth notation to N, adds acknowledgements, and reorganizes the appendices: the original full-results discussion moves from Appendix A to E, following the new studies and retained ablations.

P2.justification: V2 adds four tables and a GAT architecture diagram, and replaces the four-panel depth plot with a six-panel plot. Figures 1 and 2 are redrawn, Table 1 is reformatted, and retained figures and tables are relocated, including the full-results table moving from Table 4 to Table 13. These substantially expand and revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 replaces an unsupported step in the central mathematical argument with a valid trace/SVD proof and substantially strengthens applicability testing through multilingual, GAT, and non-linguistic experiments. The longer-training depth analysis also addresses an important weakness of the original experiment. Broad generalizations still need qualification given Table 6's reversals, and seed and limitations-checklist statements remain inconsistent. Nevertheless, the improved formal support and broader empirical scrutiny provide a substantial net quality gain.
